C1_AUTH_DISCRIMINATION.description: HTTP fingerprint discrimination > 0.5 on auth-state changes (positive control, replicates EXP-RUNTIME-33902315583)

C2_BEHAVIORAL_TP.description: Behavioral signal TP >= 0.85 on auth drift detection (JWT/session validation)

C3_ORTHOGONALITY.description: Structural+behavioral orthogonality confirmed at delta=0.15 (TOST CI upper < 0.15, Pearson r computed with non-constant input)
C3_ORTHOGONALITY.observed: FAIL: behavioral variance = 0.0 across all 720 co-occurring samples; Pearson r undefined (NaN); TOST cannot assess equivalence

C4_NOISE_FP.description: Noise FP rate <= 0.15 on structural noise samples (null control)

B_FRESHNESS_STRUCTURAL.description: HTTP fingerprint substrate discrimination on real SPIDER kernel endpoints (from EXP-RUNTIME-33902315583)

B_FRESHNESS_BEHAVIORAL.description: JWT/session validation behavioral signals (from EXP-GRAPH-35353011131, TP=1.0 on stochastic mock)

observations: Auth-state discrimination (0.8333) replicates EXP-RUNTIME-33902315583 exactly: 4 unique fingerprints, no_auth/valid_token/expired/invalid produce distinct HTTP responses
Behavioral TP rate is 1.0 for all three drift types (permission_boundary, session_invalidation, token_refresh), meaning the behavioral signal correctly identifies drift in every sample
Behavioral score is CONSTANT at 0.5 across ALL 720 co-occurring samples (std=0.0), making Pearson correlation undefined (NaN)

The behavioral_score function assigns 0.5 to permission_boundary (role=viewer +0.3, permissions<=1 +0.2) and session_invalidation (error=session_invalidated +0.3, permissions<=1 +0.2), producing identical scores for different drift mechanisms
Structural variance is non-zero (7.7431), confirming the structural signal DOES vary across conditions, but the behavioral signal does not
Noise FP rate is 0.0: structural noise (field additions, type normalization, description changes) never triggers behavioral false positives
Expired and invalid tokens produce identical fingerprints (137257c6fb39bf53), reducing inter-group discrimination from theoretical 1.0 to 0.8333
All measurements use localhost WSGI mock server (not Flask), JWT HS256, deterministic seed=42
validity_notes: This experiment tests a mock SPIDER kernel, not production endpoints. Generalization to real kernel auth/session behavior is unmeasured.
The behavioral_score function is a simplified heuristic (session_valid + role + status + permissions signals). A production behavioral signal may use different scoring.

The behavioral signal's constant score of 0.5 is an artifact of the scoring weights: permission_boundary and session_invalidation each accumulate exactly 0.5 from orthogonal signal components that happen to sum to the same value.

Orthogonality C3 FAILS not because the signals are correlated, but because the behavioral signal has zero variance. This is a measurement design issue, not a scientific finding about signal independence.
The experiment uses N=60 per condition (720 total co-occurring samples), exceeding the frozen N>=480 requirement.
Server-side state is protected by threading.Lock but requests are sequential from the main thread, so no race conditions were observed.

The 403 response for session_invalidation bypasses the noise application block (noise only applied when status_code==200), so session_invalidation co-occurring samples have no noise in the response body.
unresolved: Why does the behavioral_score function produce a constant 0.5 across all three drift types? The scoring weights (0.3+0.2 for permission_boundary, 0.3+0.2 for session_invalidation, 0.05+0.15+0.2 for token_refresh) happen to produce near-identical sums. A production behavioral signal would need differentiated scoring.

Can orthogonality be assessed with a behavioral signal that produces a continuous (non-binary) score? The current signal is effectively binary (0.5 for drift, 0.25 for no-drift), which limits correlation analysis.
Would a different behavioral scoring function (e.g., weighted by drift severity) produce sufficient variance for orthogonality testing?
Does the expired/invalid token fingerprint collision (identical 401 responses) affect production discrimination if real endpoints return different error details?

The C3 failure is a MEASUREMENT INVALIDITY (constant behavioral score prevents orthogonality assessment), not a scientific falsification of signal independence. Should C3 be redefined to test with a behavioral signal that has sufficient variance?
